title: Scientists Said Only Humans and Birds Keep a Beat. Then Ronan
subject: sea lion

scenes.text: Scientists once believed only humans and a few birds could keep a beat.
Then a rescued sea lion named Ronan joined a lab at UC Santa Cruz.
She was taught to bob her head to a rhythm. It took a few months.
Then she matched new songs she'd never heard, including Boogie Wonderland.
A 2025 study found her timing was off by only five to ten milliseconds, about a tenth of an eye blink.
Sea lions can't mimic voices, so the old theory about beat and mimicry had a problem.
